AstroGenetics: the physics behind each reading

One law runs under every reading here: a mark held against thermal noise costs energy, and the loss of that hold shows as entropy, in bits. Each reading is a ratio to its healthy reference, so healthy reads 1. Its gauge runs from 0, the floor (below it a cell can no longer hold its identity), to saturation, the most the scale can register (every identity site fully scrambled). Both ends are derived from physics, not fitted to data.

InstrumentWhat was measuredThe physics
Met-ANo reading: the noise gate withheld the state on this array (noise index 0.17179 > 0.149 and no same-run tare; A printed as a number only).A reading is given only when enough of the array's noise sites are measured to show the array is clean enough to read.
C-ScoreHow the departures of Met-A's identity sites cluster along the genome: the variance of the means of blocks of 10 neighboring sites over the variance of single sites, divided by the healthy median; C = 0.969.A ratio of clustering, so it has no derived floor or ceiling. Healthy reads near 1; the Normal band 0.877 to 1.152 was set on 617 healthy arrays from 19 studies and held in two laboratories that had no part in setting it. The sky below shows the same departures.

What changed: the sample laid over its healthy reference

The sample on the globe, against its healthy reference

Open the globe on its own full page (the same layers, larger, on a dark background).


The readings, in plain words

Each gauge runs from 0, the floor (below it a cell can no longer hold its identity), through 1, healthy, to saturation, the most the scale can register. Healthy cells sit in the green band around 1. Moving right means the marks are being lost.

Which cells are in the sample

Neutrophils 47 %, CD4 T cells 23 %, CD8 T cells 10 %, NK cells 8 %, read against the 79-cell IAM-Atlas v2.1.

Met-A

No reading on this sample: the array's own noise check could not confirm it was clean enough to read, so Met-A held back rather than guess.

C-Score

Whether the changes are scattered, as in healthy cells, or clustered along the genome.

The sample on the sphere

Each dot of color is one place in the genome. Speckle is what healthy looks like; patches mean the changes are bunched together.
